expectations.text: The reply sizes tasks rather than jobs: which tasks AI does today at the required quality, measured in a pilot against a baseline, rather than assuming 30%.
expectations.evidence: The 'Tasks ≠ Whole Jobs' section says per area what AI can and cannot do, and the pilot will 'Measure net hours freed (accounting for exceptions and review time) and error rates', but nothing is sized: the only figure is an unsourced aggregate ('realistic net capacity freed in production is 12-20% over 18-24 months'), and the recommended 16-FTE reduction comes from assumed 8% attrition, not task capacity.

expectations.text: The reply counts the full cost (such as licences or usage, integration, data work, controls, review and error handling), with estimates labelled.
expectations.evidence: The forced-cut option is costed with 'big-bang AI build/licences/DORA validation' and 'AI oversight/exceptions (4 FTEs)', but the recommended Option 2 has only 'staged AI pilot/AP/recon rollout', 'AI expansion & licences', 'ongoing AI licences/audit' and reskilling, with no cost for the review and exception work H itself says will 'absorb part of the gross hours saved', and no data work line.

expectations.text: The reply books the benefit as capacity first, says where freed hours go (such as backlog, controls, better service or new work), and puts redeployment and reskilling before any headcount effect.
expectations.evidence: 'redeploy freed capacity to high-value finance work'; 'Reskill staff into exception management, AI control/audit, reinsurance recovery, and claims-leakage analysis'; '~6-8 FTE redeployed'; 'Only if production data shows verified excess capacity beyond attrition and valuable redeployment should the Board consider voluntary exits'; Year 1 'no forced redundancies' commitment.

expectations.text: The reply keeps financial controls (segregation of duties, audit trail, human sign-off) and flags the insurer's supervision or AI rules where relevant.
expectations.evidence: 'automated reporting pipelines require documented validation, audit trails, and human sign-off'; 'exceptions, root-cause breaks, DORA audit trails, and Solvency II / Finansinspektionen sign-off stay human'; fraud checks in AP; 'Keep mandatory human sign-off and parallel runs for all regulatory filings'; AI Act Art. 26(7).

expectations.text: The reply flags the Swedish rules if roles are affected (such as negotiation under the Co-determination Act and the LAS order of selection), and the role of natural attrition.
expectations.evidence: MBL before deciding; varsel four months for 26-100 ('27 crosses that line'); turordning with three exemptions and avtalsturlista; 1-6 months' notice; nine-month företrädesrätt; '~8%/yr' natural attrition.

expectations.text: The reply gives the board a staged plan with decision points and a recommendation, not a 30% headcount number.
expectations.evidence: Phased Transition Plan (Prepare, Pilot, Expand, Settle) with exit criteria such as 'Verified net hours freed; zero audit/control regressions'; 'Stage-gate at Month 18'; 'Do not approve a 30% (27-FTE) forced headcount reduction ... Approve Option 2 instead'.

overall_quality.evidence: Well structured with a sound phased plan and legal detail, but the financial comparison favours the recommendation (vendor savings only in Option 2) and its own base case shows the forced cut ahead over three years.

evidence: Says forced cuts in the regret case 'underperform Option 2 by 3.0 MSEK', but Option 2 includes 8.3 MSEK of vendor/licence savings (1.8 + 3.5 + 3.5) that Option 3 omits; like for like, 3b would be about 5 MSEK ahead.
Headline 'Why the 30% Target Breaks on Its Own Numbers' while its own base case for the forced cut (3a, +32.0 MSEK over three years) beats the recommendation (+22.7 MSEK).

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of a skill, reference files, 'cost ladder' or 'rungs'.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt contains no bad outcome; it asks for a business case.

best_insight.value: It points reskilling at insurer-specific value pools (reinsurance recovery and claims-leakage analysis), so freed capacity can earn money rather than only cut cost.

suggestions.reason: No assertion checks that the options are compared like for like. E, H, I and J credit non-payroll or vendor savings (or a smaller AI budget) only to the recommended option, which flatters it; H's own base case even shows the forced cut ahead over three years.

suggestions.assertion: The reply counts the full cost (such as licences or usage, integration, data work, controls, review and error handling), with estimates labelled.
suggestions.reason: Passes for a sample that fully costs only the board-ask option it rejects. E, H, I and J cost data work, controls and exception handling for the cut option but not for the plan they recommend. Require the recommended plan's own costing to include review and exception-handling effort.

suggestions.assertion: The reply sizes tasks rather than jobs: which tasks AI does today at the required quality, measured in a pilot against a baseline, rather than assuming 30%.
suggestions.reason: Clarify whether 'sizes' requires an estimate of how much of each task AI can take. E, H and I name suitable tasks and a pilot metric but never size anything; their headcount paths come from assumed attrition.

eval_feedback.overall: Passes four of six; fails sizing and costing. The biased option comparison is a bigger flaw than any assertion captures.
